title: Auth0 Pricing 2026: Plans, Tiers and Monthly Costs
summary: Auth0 pricing has a free tier, self-serve paid tiers, and an Enterprise plan available by quote. Compare feature limits and monthly costs across all three.
body_markdown:
## Automate Auth0 user tasks with Activepieces


Activepieces can take over the glue code you wrote around Auth0 (onboarding, offboarding, syncing users to a CRM, Slack or billing), and with 746 integrations, roughly 60% of them community-contributed, the tool on the other end of each sync is usually already covered.


It does nothing to Auth0's price, and that's the right way to size it.


### Where workflows fit around Auth0


Activepieces charges 1 credit per flow run, however many steps the flow has, so an offboarding flow split into ten small steps costs the same as the two-step shortcut it replaced. Zapier bills per task, which means every extra step adds to the invoice.


Here the run is the meter and the steps inside it are yours to arrange. The useful question's how many hand-written scripts you currently maintain to react to Auth0 events.


When a new signup creates a CRM contact, posts to a Slack channel and opens a billing record, that's three pieces of custom code, each with its own credentials and failure modes.


In a workflow builder, that becomes one trigger followed by three actions you can read at a glance.


The screenshot shows the shape of it with a different trigger. It's a three-step flow named "Calendly Tracking," where a Calendly "Event Canceled" trigger feeds a Slack message and a Gmail email.


Swap the trigger for an Auth0 event and the pattern's the same, one event fanning out to the tools your team already uses. What to take from it's the maintenance model: changing a step means editing a block and pressing Publish, not redeploying a service.


Offboarding benefits most. Removing a departing user from Auth0, notifying the team and closing the billing record can run as one flow instead of a checklist someone forgets.


Activepieces can also be self-hosted, and its core is MIT-licensed, so the free Community Edition keeps the automation layer from becoming another metered vendor line beside your identity bill.


### What it doesn't change


Your Auth0 bill's still driven by monthly active users, the enterprise features you need and the quote you get at the top of the self-serve tiers.


Activepieces sits outside that calculation, with a separate free plan at $0 that includes 1,000 credits a month and unlimited flows.


Before you plan to retire any code, check that the events and actions you rely on're covered, because Activepieces' Auth0 connection's modest.


Its source sits in the packages/integrations/community folder of the open source monorepo on GitHub, so you can read the listed triggers and actions before committing.


If your real concern's lock-in, moving user sync into workflows doesn't move your users out of Auth0. It only makes your surrounding logic easier to rewire when you do.
